source.anchor: AppendixB2.2 Ex60: explicit radial integral on RHS of first equality, Gaussian evaluation in second equality; p4.4 and Eq21 genuine B6 specialization. Standing assumptions AppendixB2; B6 Eq15.
source.original_text: Let n>=3, kappa>=4 and lambda>=0, and draw O from the existing normalized Haar probability on the full real O(n). Put U=O_11, p=n/2 as a real number, a(O)=kappa+1+4lambda-(kappa-1)U, A_O=((kappa+1)/2)I-((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T), F(O)=det(O)sqrt(det A_O), N(O)=(sqrt(kappa)+1)U-(sqrt(kappa)-1), and J(O)=integral over real Euclidean n-space of exp(-a(O)||x||^2/4) against canonical volume. Every inner spatial integrand is absolutely integrable; F(O)J(O) and N(O)/a(O)^p are absolutely integrable under this Haar probability. Their finite expectations satisfy E[FJ]/(2pi)^p = [(-1)^(n-1)(sqrt(kappa)-1)^(n-1)/2^p] E[N/a^p]. This evaluates the explicit radialized iterated integral and does not identify it with the original mixture test H(lambda).

decoder_context: Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) R is the full real orthogonal group, with the inherited finite real matrix topology and its Borel sigma-algebra, allowing both determinant signs. Compactness and second countability are supplied internally.
Measure.haarMeasure on top is the actual normalized Haar measure on the whole compact group and has total mass one; it is not an arbitrary measure, special-orthogonal law or conditional law.
EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) carries its Euclidean norm and canonical volume. Its real dimension is n. An integral with no explicit measure in this statement uses this volume.

All displayed lets are literal abbreviations. The first coordinate is the zero-based index0, whose membership proof follows from the dimension inequality. Real.sqrt is the nonnegative real square root. Real powers have real exponent p=(n:R)/2; sign powers n-1 have natural exponents.

Integrable denotes actual absolute Bochner L1 integrability under the displayed measure. The proposition explicitly includes spatial integrability for every matrix and both indicated outer Haar integrability conclusions; it is an identity for the displayed iterated integral itself.

/-!
# The radialized Gaussian test integral

Zhou--Suzuki arXiv:2610.20492v1, Appendix B.2.2, Ex60 and Eq21.
This evaluates the displayed explicit iterated integral, with genuine L1
conclusions, using the existing full Haar law and actual Lemma B.6.
Identification with the original H(lambda), actual Gaussian probability laws,
conjugation/radialization, Fubini, spherical Poisson and TV are separate.
-/

open Matrix MeasureTheory Set TopologicalSpace
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.OrthogonalHaar
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.DeterminantFamily
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.DeterminantCancellation

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.RadialIntegral

private lemma integrable_continuous_haar {n : ℕ}
    {f : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Continuous f) :
    Integrable f (orthogonalHaar n) := by
  let := (orthogonalHaar_spec n).1
  exact hf.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport (isClosed_tsupport f).isCompact

private lemma gaussian_integral {n : ℕ} {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) :
    Integrable (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) => Real.exp (-a * ‖x‖ ^ 2 / 4)) volume ∧
      (∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), Real.exp (-a * ‖x‖ ^ 2 / 4)) =
        (4 * Real.pi / a) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) := by
  have hb : 0 < ((a / 4 : ℝ) : ℂ).re := by simpa using (show 0 < a / 4 by positivity)
  have hc := GaussianFourier.integrable_cexp_neg_mul_sq_norm_add
    (V := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) hb 0 0
  have hi := GaussianFourier.integral_rexp_neg_mul_sq_norm
    (V := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (b := a / 4) (by positivity)
  have he (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :
      -(a / 4) * ‖x‖ ^ 2 = -a * ‖x‖ ^ 2 / 4 := by ring
  constructor
  · convert hc.re using 1
    funext x
    simp only [zero_mul, add_zero]
    rw [← Complex.ofReal_pow, ← Complex.ofReal_neg, ← Complex.ofReal_mul,
      ← Complex.ofReal_exp]
    change Real.exp (-a * ‖x‖ ^ 2 / 4) = Real.exp (-(a / 4) * ‖x‖ ^ 2)
    exact congrArg Real.exp (he x).symm
  · have hp : Real.pi / (a / 4) = 4 * Real.pi / a := by ring
    simpa only [he, finrank_euclideanSpace, Fintype.card_fin, hp] using hi


theorem radialized_test_integral {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) {κ : ℝ}
    (hκ : 4 ≤ κ) {ℓ : ℝ} (hℓ : 0 ≤ ℓ) :
    let j0 : Fin n := ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩
    let U : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ :=
      fun O => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) j0 j0
    let a : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ :=
      fun O => κ + 1 + 4 * ℓ - (κ - 1) * U O
    let p : ℝ := (n : ℝ) / 2
    (∀ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
      Integrable (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) => Real.exp (-a O * ‖x‖ ^ 2 / 4)) volume) ∧
    Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ =>
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det *
        (∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), Real.exp (-a O * ‖x‖ ^ 2 / 4))) (orthogonalHaar n) ∧
    Integrable (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ =>
      ((Real.sqrt κ + 1) * U O - (Real.sqrt κ - 1)) / (a O) ^ p) (orthogonalHaar n) ∧
    (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
      (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det *
        (∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), Real.exp (-a O * ‖x‖ ^ 2 / 4)) ∂orthogonalHaar n) /
      (2 * Real.pi) ^ p =
      ((-1 : ℝ) ^ (n - 1) * (Real.sqrt κ - 1) ^ (n - 1) / (2 : ℝ) ^ p) *
        (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
          ((Real.sqrt κ + 1) * U O - (Real.sqrt κ - 1)) / (a O) ^ p ∂orthogonalHaar n) := by
  classical
  let j0 : Fin n := ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩
  let U : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ :=
    fun O => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) j0 j0
  let a : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ :=
    fun O => κ + 1 + 4 * ℓ - (κ - 1) * U O
  let p : ℝ := (n : ℝ) / 2
  let F : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ :=
    fun O => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det * Real.sqrt (singleBlockPrecision κ O).det
  let N : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ :=
    fun O => (Real.sqrt κ + 1) * U O - (Real.sqrt κ - 1)
  let J : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ :=
    fun O => ∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), Real.exp (-a O * ‖x‖ ^ 2 / 4)
  let C : ℝ := (4 * Real.pi) ^ p
  let c : ℝ := (-1 : ℝ) ^ (n - 1) * (Real.sqrt κ - 1) ^ (n - 1)
  change (∀ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
      Integrable (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) => Real.exp (-a O * ‖x‖ ^ 2 / 4)) volume) ∧
    Integrable (fun O => F O * J O) (orthogonalHaar n) ∧
    Integrable (fun O => N O / (a O) ^ p) (orthogonalHaar n) ∧
      (∫ O, F O * J O ∂orthogonalHaar n) / (2 * Real.pi) ^ p =
        (c / (2 : ℝ) ^ p) * (∫ O, N O / (a O) ^ p ∂orthogonalHaar n)
  have hUc : Continuous U := continuous_subtype_val.matrix_elem j0 j0
  have hac : Continuous a := by dsimp only [a]; fun_prop
  have ha_bound (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) : 2 + 4 * ℓ ≤ a O := by
    have hU : U O ≤ 1 := le_trans (le_abs_self _) (by
      simpa only [U, Real.norm_eq_abs] using entry_norm_bound_of_unitary O.property j0 j0)
    have hmul := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hU (show 0 ≤ κ - 1 by linarith)
    dsimp only [a]
    nlinarith
  have ha_pos (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) : 0 < a O := by
    have := ha_bound O
    linarith
  have hpownz (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) : (a O) ^ p ≠ 0 :=
    (Real.rpow_pos_of_pos (ha_pos O) p).ne'
  have hpowc : Continuous (fun O => (a O) ^ p) :=
    hac.rpow_const (fun O => Or.inl (ha_pos O).ne')
  have hAc : Continuous (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ => singleBlockPrecision κ O) := by
    unfold singleBlockPrecision
    exact continuous_const.sub
      ((continuous_subtype_val.add continuous_subtype_val.matrix_transpose).const_smul ((κ - 1) / 4))
  have hFc : Continuous F := continuous_subtype_val.matrix_det.mul
    (Real.continuous_sqrt.comp hAc.matrix_det)
  have hNc : Continuous N := (hUc.const_mul _).sub continuous_const
  have hWint : Integrable (fun O => F O / (a O) ^ p) (orthogonalHaar n) :=
    integrable_continuous_haar (hFc.div hpowc hpownz)
  have hNint : Integrable (fun O => N O / (a O) ^ p) (orthogonalHaar n) :=
    integrable_continuous_haar (hNc.div hpowc hpownz)
  have hJ (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) : J O = (4 * Real.pi / a O) ^ p :=
    (gaussian_integral (ha_pos O)).2
  have hprod (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) :
      F O * J O = C * (F O / (a O) ^ p) := by
    rw [hJ, Real.div_rpow (by positivity) (ha_pos O).le]
    dsimp only [C]
    ring
  have hOuter : Integrable (fun O => F O * J O) (orthogonalHaar n) :=
    (hWint.const_mul C).congr (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun O => (hprod O).symm)
  refine ⟨fun O => (gaussian_integral (ha_pos O)).1, hOuter, hNint, ?_⟩
  let h : ℝ → ℝ := fun u => 1 / (max (κ + 1 + 4 * ℓ - (κ - 1) * u) 1) ^ p
  have hbase : Continuous (fun u : ℝ => max (κ + 1 + 4 * ℓ - (κ - 1) * u) 1) := by fun_prop
  have hbase_pos (u : ℝ) : 0 < max (κ + 1 + 4 * ℓ - (κ - 1) * u) 1 :=
    lt_of_lt_of_le zero_lt_one (le_max_right _ _)
  have hh : Continuous h := continuous_const.div
    (hbase.rpow_const (fun u => Or.inl (hbase_pos u).ne'))
    (fun u => (Real.rpow_pos_of_pos (hbase_pos u) p).ne')
  have hactual (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) : h (U O) = 1 / (a O) ^ p := by
    change 1 / (max (a O) 1) ^ p = 1 / (a O) ^ p
    rw [max_eq_left (by linarith [ha_bound O])]
  have hL1 : Integrable (fun O => h (U O)) (orthogonalHaar n) :=
    integrable_continuous_haar (hh.comp hUc)
  have hb := signed_sqrt_det_integral hn hκ h hh.measurable hL1
  change (∫ O, F O * h (U O) ∂orthogonalHaar n) =
    c / (2 : ℝ) ^ n * (∫ O, N O * h (U O) ∂orthogonalHaar n) at hb
  simp_rw [hactual, mul_one_div] at hb
  have hOuter_eq : (∫ O, F O * J O ∂orthogonalHaar n) =
      C * (∫ O, F O / (a O) ^ p ∂orthogonalHaar n) := by
    simp_rw [hprod]
    exact integral_const_mul _ _
  have hpi_ne : (2 * Real.pi) ^ p ≠ 0 :=
    (Real.rpow_pos_of_pos (by positivity : 0 < 2 * Real.pi) p).ne'
  have htwo_ne : (2 : ℝ) ^ p ≠ 0 := (Real.rpow_pos_of_pos (by norm_num : 0 < (2 : ℝ)) p).ne'
  have hnorm : C / (2 * Real.pi) ^ p = (2 : ℝ) ^ p := by
    dsimp only [C]
    rw [show 4 * Real.pi = (2 : ℝ) * (2 * Real.pi) by ring,
      Real.mul_rpow (by norm_num : 0 ≤ (2 : ℝ)) (by positivity)]
    exact mul_div_cancel_right₀ _ hpi_ne
  have htwos : (2 : ℝ) ^ n = (2 : ℝ) ^ p * (2 : ℝ) ^ p := by
    rw [← Real.rpow_natCast, ← Real.rpow_add (by norm_num : 0 < (2 : ℝ))]
    congr 1
    dsimp only [p]
    ring
  rw [hOuter_eq]
  calc
    C * (∫ O, F O / (a O) ^ p ∂orthogonalHaar n) / (2 * Real.pi) ^ p =
        (C / (2 * Real.pi) ^ p) * (∫ O, F O / (a O) ^ p ∂orthogonalHaar n) := by ring
    _ = (2 : ℝ) ^ p * (c / (2 : ℝ) ^ n *
        (∫ O, N O / (a O) ^ p ∂orthogonalHaar n)) := by rw [hnorm, hb]
    _ = c / (2 : ℝ) ^ p * (∫ O, N O / (a O) ^ p ∂orthogonalHaar n) := by
      rw [htwos]
      field_simp [htwo_ne]

steps.title: Keep the denominator strictly positive
steps.text: Orthogonality bounds the first diagonal entry by one in absolute value. Since kappa-1 is nonnegative, a(O)>=2+4lambda>=2. Thus every real power and denominator in the displayed actual integrands has a strictly positive base. This is derived from the stated assumptions.
steps.lean: The main proof uses entry_norm_bound_of_unitary on the actual matrix, then ha_bound and ha_pos. No caller bound or regularity premise is added.

steps.title: Evaluate a genuine finite spatial Gaussian integral
steps.text: For each fixed O, apply the existing Euclidean Gaussian formula with positive rate a(O)/4. Its integrability theorem is used as well as its value. Dimension is exactly n, and the exponent is n/2 in R. Hence this step cannot obtain the displayed value from a default integral of a divergent function.
steps.lean: Private gaussian_integral genuinely calls GaussianFourier.integrable_cexp_neg_mul_sq_norm_add and takes its real part, then GaussianFourier.integral_rexp_neg_mul_sq_norm. Canonical finrank_euclideanSpace identifies dimension n. This is reuse of Mathlib, not a new public generic Gaussian wrapper.

steps.title: Prove the outer expectations are finite
steps.text: The functions U, a, det(O), det(A_O) and sqrt(det(A_O)) are continuous on the actual compact group O(n). The positive denominators preserve continuity. Thus F/a^p and N/a^p are integrable under the existing finite Haar probability. The formula for J transfers integrability to FJ. The implementation uses finite compact bounds where explicit sharp domination constants are unnecessary.
steps.lean: Private integrable_continuous_haar consumes orthogonalHaar_spec and Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport on compact O(n). The main proof establishes continuity of the literal precision and positive real-power denominators. This does not perform Fubini on the original experiment.

steps.title: Extract the exact Gaussian normalization
steps.text: Use the pointwise finite Gaussian formula inside the already defined iterated integral. Real-power multiplication and quotient rules give (4pi)^p/(2pi)^p=2^p. Moving this constant through the Haar integral is ordinary one-integral linearity; no exchange of two integrals is asserted.
steps.lean: hprod and hOuter_eq use the actual gaussian_integral value, Real.div_rpow and integral_const_mul. hnorm proves the pi factors cancel exactly.

steps.title: Apply the actual general L1 cancellation theorem
steps.text: Choose a globally continuous scalar extension h(u)=1/max(kappa+1+4lambda-(kappa-1)u,1)^p. On every actual U, the denominator is at least two, so h(U)=1/a(O)^p exactly. This extension makes the real-line Borel condition explicit without changing the actual weight. Compactness gives its actual Haar L1 property. The existing LemmaB6 therefore applies with all its genuine hypotheses discharged.
steps.lean: The proof constructs the continuous positive-base max extension, proves hactual on every O and hL1 internally, and directly calls the identical compiled signed_sqrt_det_integral. The extension is a proof adapter outside the actual entry range, not a changed source weight or source repair.

steps.title: Retain the half-dimensional power and sign
steps.text: Since p=n/2 is real division, 2p=n and 2^n=2^p 2^p. Multiplying the Gaussian factor by the exact B6 coefficient gives 2^p/2^n=1/2^p. The parity factor (-1)^(n-1) and power (sqrt(kappa)-1)^(n-1) are unchanged.
steps.lean: htwos uses Real.rpow_add and Real.rpow_natCast with p+p=n. The final field identity uses actual nonzero positive powers; no natural-number truncation of n/2 is allowed.

reconstruction.text:
For every natural number n with 3 ≤ n, every real number κ with 4 ≤ κ, and every real number ℓ with 0 ≤ ℓ, make the following definitions. Let j₀ = 0 be the first coordinate in Fin n = {0,…,n−1}. Let G = O(n) = {O ∈ ℝ^{n×n} : OᵀO = Iₙ} be the full real orthogonal group, including both determinant signs, with its inherited finite-matrix topology and Borel σ-algebra. Let μ be the normalized Haar measure on G, so μ(G) = 1. Identify E = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with ℝⁿ, equipped with its Euclidean norm and canonical n-dimensional volume dx. Define U : G → ℝ by U(O) = O_{j₀j₀}, define a : G → ℝ by a(O) = κ + 1 + 4ℓ − (κ − 1)U(O), and let p = (n as a real number)/2 ∈ ℝ. For notation in the conclusions, write B(O) = ((κ + 1)/2)Iₙ − ((κ − 1)/4)(O + Oᵀ).

Then all of the following conclusions hold simultaneously:
(1) For every O ∈ G, the real function x ↦ exp(−a(O)‖x‖²/4) on E is absolutely Bochner L¹-integrable with respect to dx.
(2) The real function O ↦ det(O) sqrt(det(B(O))) [∫_E exp(−a(O)‖x‖²/4) dx] is absolutely Bochner L¹-integrable with respect to μ.
(3) The real function O ↦ ((sqrt(κ) + 1)U(O) − (sqrt(κ) − 1))/a(O)^p is absolutely Bochner L¹-integrable with respect to μ.
(4) The following exact identity holds for the indicated iterated integral:

[∫_G det(O) sqrt(det(((κ + 1)/2)Iₙ − ((κ − 1)/4)(O + Oᵀ))) [∫_E exp(−a(O)‖x‖²/4) dx] dμ(O)]/(2π)^p
= [(-1)^(n−1) (sqrt(κ) − 1)^(n−1)/2^p] [∫_G ((sqrt(κ) + 1)U(O) − (sqrt(κ) − 1))/a(O)^p dμ(O)].

Every square root denotes the nonnegative real square root. Every power with exponent p uses the real exponent p = n/2, including when n is odd; each power with exponent n−1 has the natural exponent n−1. The inner integral is over x and canonical volume, and every outer integral is over the whole group G with the same normalized Haar measure μ. There are no hypotheses of spatial or outer integrability: the three L¹ assertions above are part of the conclusion.
